title: Care Assistant - Bank - Care Home
description:
This is a Bank role so no confirmed hours

Shifts -8am to 8pm or 8pm to 8am

We are not accepting sponsorships or switch

ABOUT THE ROLE
This is a casual, part-time role offering flexible working. As a Bank Care Assistant at a Barchester care home, you'll help residents enjoy each day by making sure they get the quality care and support they deserve. You'll assist with daily living, providing support and companionship and sharing great moments and memories too. It's a chance to bring your dedication and compassion to a fulfilling environment. Every day will be different, so you can expect to undertake work that's as varied as it is rewarding. As a Bank Care Assistant, you could be doing anything from supporting residents with their food and drink and following care plans to ensuring that each of our residents has one-to-one time. It's an opportunity to put your skills to meaningful use and develop your career.

ABOUT YOU
To join us as a Bank Care Assistant you'll need to have some experience of caring for older people, a can-do approach and excellent communication skills. Your empathy and warm-hearted approach will shine through, but above all, you'll have the compassion needed to deliver the highest standard of care and support for all our residents. In return we'll provide all the training you need to thrive.

REWARDS PACKAGE
As well as competitive pay, you can look forward to a role that offers true flexibility and plenty of free learning and development opportunities. As one of the UK's leading healthcare providers, we take the growth of everyone who works for us seriously.

As this is a Bank position to provide cover as and when we need it, such as for annual leave or sick leave, the hours and days you work will vary.

If you'd like to use your people skills in an organisation that provides the quality care you'd expect for your loved ones, this is a rewarding place to be.

title: Support Worker
description:
Support Worker

Location: Clouds House

Salary: £28,479 per annum

About the Role

We are looking for a compassionate, reliable and motivated Support Worker to join our team at Clouds House, helping to create and maintain a safe, structured and recovery-focused residential environment.

This is a rewarding, hands-on role where you will play an important part in supporting individuals throughout their treatment and recovery journey. You will help ensure that the residential environment remains safe, stable and therapeutic, enabling clients to engage fully with their recovery programme.

Working closely with the wider team and reporting to the Support Worker Team Leader, you will provide both practical and therapeutic support, encouraging positive engagement, promoting independence and reinforcing the principles of our 12-Step recovery model and trauma-informed approach.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing consistent, compassionate and recovery-focused support to clients throughout their residential treatment journey.
- Maintaining a visible and supportive presence across the residential setting, helping to promote safety, structure and positive communal living.
- Encouraging client engagement with the treatment programme and reinforcing the values and principles of the 12-Step model.
- Maintaining appropriate professional boundaries and demonstrating emotional resilience and effective communication.
- Supporting safeguarding, risk management and the identification and reporting of concerns.
- Undertaking medication administration responsibilities in line with organisational policies, procedures and training requirements.
- Maintaining accurate records and documentation, including the use of electronic medication administration systems (eMAR).
- Promoting high standards of health and safety, cleanliness and infection prevention and control.
- Working collaboratively with colleagues to ensure a consistent, trauma-informed and therapeutic approach across all shifts.

This is an opportunity to be part of a dedicated team where your contribution genuinely matters and where every day offers the chance to make a positive difference.

About You

You will be a caring, approachable and dependable individual who is passionate about supporting people to achieve lasting recovery and positive change.

You will understand the importance of creating a safe, respectful and supportive environment, while recognising the need for consistency, structure and clear professional boundaries when working with individuals who may have experienced trauma, addiction and complex life challenges.

We are looking for someone who:
- Has experience working in health and social care, recovery services or residential support settings.
- Has an understanding of safeguarding principles and the importance of promoting the safety and wellbeing of vulnerable adults.
- Demonstrates a genuine commitment to recovery-focused and trauma-informed practice.
- Has strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to build positive and professional relationships.
- Can remain calm, emotionally regulated and professional when managing challenging situations.
- Is confident working independently and as part of a wider multidisciplinary team.
- Understands the importance of accurate record-keeping, accountability and following policies and procedures.
- Is flexible, reliable and willing to undertake the training required to fulfil the responsibilities of the role.

A Care Certificate is desirable, or you should be willing to work towards completing one. You should also be willing to undertake training in electronic medication administration (eMAR) and Immediate Life Support (ILS), if not already qualified.

Most importantly, you will bring compassion, resilience and a genuine belief that people can change.

If you are passionate about helping people rebuild their lives and want to be part of a supportive team delivering life-changing residential treatment, we would love to hear from you.

Join The Forward Trust and help people move forward into a brighter future.

About Us

We are The Forward Trust, the social enterprise with charitable status that empowers people to break the often interlinked cycles of crime and addiction to move forward with their lives. For more than 25 years we have been working with people to build positive and productive lives, whatever their past. We believe that anyone is capable of lasting change. Our services have supported thousands of people to make positive changes and build productive lives with a job, family, friends and a sense of community.

Please note that we may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications.

Please note that remote roles may require occasional travel for site visits, training and meetings.

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Forward Trust, please click apply to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

title: Support Worker
description:
Support Worker

Care Connection are recruiting, experienced Support Workers, to support our clients in the Trowbridge area!

As an Agency Support Worker, you will be working across a variety of supported living services in the area, supporting individuals with varying support needs, from those with autism, learning difficulties and behaviours that may challenge to individuals who may require extra support around their mental health needs.

Shifts here can be variable between 07.00-22.00 and sleep ins.

Job Role:

A Support Worker is required to deliver support within an adult's health or social care environment, supporting with daily living tasks or development of new skills. The tasks may be one to one with an adult or with other support workers or health professionals, they may be provided within the home and garden itself or outside in the community, equipment may be required for moving and handling or health tasks. A support plan on site must be followed for completion of tasks, safety, client communication and any end-of-life instruction where relevant.

Benefits:

Weekly pay from 13.00- 14.00 per hour shift dependent

Holiday accrued as you work

Perks at work benefit scheme, offering a wide range of savings and benefits, from shopping and holidays, to health and wellbeing solutions

Shifts ranging from days and nights to weekends

Flexible working hours around your own availability

Induction and refresher training

On call support

The Best Connection is acting as an Employment Business in relation to this vacancy.

title: Healthcare Assistant
description:
Role Overview

Affinity Staff is recruiting compassionate and reliable Healthcare Assistants (HCAs) to join our agency team, supporting an established care facility in Calne, Wiltshire.

As a temporary HCA working through Affinity Staff, you will play a vital role in providing high-quality personal care, dignity, and companionship to residents. You will enjoy complete control over your schedule while benefiting from our dedicated, round-the-clock support.

Key Responsibilities
- Assisting residents with daily personal care, dressing, hygiene, and mobility needs.
- Supporting meal times, nutrition monitoring, and encouraging hydration.
- Promoting dignity, independence, and person-centred care at all times.
- Maintaining accurate care records and daily fluid/food intake documentation.
- Collaborating with senior carers and nursing staff to ensure a safe, supportive environment.

Requirements
- Minimum 6 months of experience in a UK healthcare or care home setting.
- NVQ Level 2 in Health & Social Care (preferred but not essential).
- Enhanced DBS check registered on the Update Service (or willing to process a new one).
- Valid Right to Work in the UK.
- Caring, reliable nature with excellent communication skills.

Benefits of Working with Affinity Staff
- Competitive Market Rates with prompt weekly pay.
- 24/7 Support: Dedicated consultants available round-the-clock to assist you.
- Total Flexibility: Choose the shifts that fit around your lifestyle and commitments.
- Fast-track registration process and easy shift booking.

How to Apply

Click Apply Now on CV-Library to join Affinity Staff or contact the Affinity Staff recruitment team to get registered immediately.
